title: KP14 U-shaped exposure (0.28, 0, 0, 0, 0.28) across a MILD visible level ladder 0.8..1.2, five types, exact compensation, price 2.5 (small firms constrained, large firms operationally levered)
question: Does a U-shaped loading across size give KP14 room and a fair gap at the bar?
notes:
WHY (2026-11-01). A non-monotone exposure with a simple story, built the same way in every model: five equal types on the mild visible level ladder 0.8..1.2 with the loading U-shaped across it, b = (0.28, 0, 0, 0, 0.28), exact y = 0 compensation (bv_comp 1.0) so that only size carries the U. Small firms are exposed to the aggregate cash-flow shock through financing constraints, large firms through operating leverage, mid-sized firms through neither. The hump twins (bvyhx4 / vyhx4 / gvyhx4, b = -c, 0, +c, 0, -c) are running; the U has no sign flip and all its exposure is of one sign, so its mean is not zero and the market holds the common part; the room is the curvature in size, which no linear function of the characteristics spans (bvyvee's V across the WIDE ladder 0.6..1.4 failed because the level's own monotone premium swamped it; the mild ladder and the larger loading are bvyhx3/4's fix).
